name: GA-13
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The seat sits in a heavily Democratic Atlanta-area district with a +21 partisan lean, and Jasmine Clark has raised over $1.6 million with more than $4 million in outside support against a Republican challenger showing no measurable fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the Republican closing within single digits would be the main signal to revisit, though nothing currently suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Everton Blair (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
This open Atlanta-area seat is one of the most Democratic-leaning districts in Georgia, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward Democrats. Everton Blair is not on the ballot, but the Democratic nominee, Jasmine Clark, enters the general election with a decisive resource edge: roughly $1.6 million raised, $229,000 on hand, and more than $4.2 million in outside support, with no outside spending opposing her.

The Republican nominee, Jonathan Chavez, reports no fundraising or cash on hand, and no public general-election polling exists for the race. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97%. With the district's strong lean and the lopsided money gap, the race is rated Safe Democratic, with modest uncertainty from the lack of polling and the open-seat dynamic.
